correctness.rationale: The unique-blocker lemma is exact because a deleted matching gives at most one nonneighbor per vertex. Distinct blocker colors cannot coexist. Exhaustive disjoint cases for two-color, three-color unblocked, one-blocker and two-blocker configurations yield all six integer formulas. The second blocker disappears by update two because n-k>=4 implies n>=5 and at least two vertices of the formerly missing intermediate color. Direct C++ neighbor scans for 1,560,978 labelled states over 36 (n,k) cases and independent Python structural classification for 498,096 states over 30 cases reproduce all counts and F^5=F^2. Finite computations only corroborate the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The matching defect count k is an intrinsic, symmetry-independent graph perturbation parameter. Exact census separates robust eventual consensus (only +6k initial states) from immediate recurrence (loss of 2k(2^{n-2}-1) distinct cycles), while two disjoint defects interact quadratically in the sharp two-update delay class 12k(k-1). This gives a natural complete dynamical classification for a nontrivial infinite family, not a single arbitrary small graph or a generic period bound.
